metadata.title: NYU International Hospitality Industry Investment Conference
metadata.description: The NYU International Hospitality Industry Investment Conference — known widely as the NYU Hotel Conference — is the most internationally recognised...

records.body:
The NYU International Hospitality Industry Investment Conference, known widely as the NYU Hotel Conference, is the most internationally recognised gathering in the global lodging investment calendar. For more than four decades, the conference has convened at the Marriott Marquis in Times Square to bring together the most senior executives in hospitality investment from across the world.

The NYU conference is defined by its keynote conversations. Industry leaders from major hotel groups, sovereign wealth funds, private equity, and branded operators use the NYU stage to signal strategic direction and share unfiltered assessments of the global operating environment. The 2026 programme addresses the recalibration of international capital flows following two years of rate volatility, the competitive dynamics between branded and independent hotels in gateway markets, and the technology investment priorities that will define operating efficiency over the next decade.

Attendance at NYU is a signal in itself, the conference draws the CEOs, chairmen, and chief investment officers whose decisions shape the global lodging industry. The hallway conversations and dinner meetings that accompany the formal programme generate as much business activity as the sessions themselves.

records.body:
The Restaurants Canada Show is Canada's premier food service and hospitality trade event, bringing together more than 15,000 industry professionals over three days at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre. The show spans every segment of Canada's foodservice sector, from independent restaurants and hotel F&B operations to institutional catering and quick-service chains.

The 2026 edition places particular emphasis on the intersection of technology and hospitality, including AI-assisted menu engineering, integrated reservation and point-of-sale systems, and the data infrastructure that allows operators to move from intuition-based to evidence-based decision-making. For hotel food and beverage teams, the show provides unmatched access to supplier innovation across equipment, ingredients, and operational software.

The Canadian Food and Beverage Awards ceremony takes place on the final evening, recognising operators, chefs, and suppliers who have demonstrated exceptional standards and innovation in the preceding twelve months. The networking events associated with the show consistently rank among the most productive in the Canadian hospitality calendar.

metadata.title: Sustainable Hospitality Forum — New York
metadata.description: The Sustainable Hospitality Forum comes to New York this November, convening practitioners, investors, and policymakers working at the intersection of...

records.body:
The Sustainable Hospitality Forum comes to New York this November, convening practitioners, investors, and policymakers working at the intersection of environmental sustainability and hospitality operations.

This is not a forum for aspirations. Every session is built around specific case studies, what was done, what it cost, what it delivered, and structured to produce takeaways that participants can apply in their own organisations immediately.

The 2026 programme covers four principal themes: decarbonisation pathways for hotel portfolios, the business case for circular economy practices in food and beverage, sustainable luxury, reconciling premium positioning with environmental responsibility, and regulatory compliance as strategic opportunity.

The New York edition reflects the city's position as both a major hospitality market and an increasingly demanding regulatory environment. New York City's Local Law 97, which mandates carbon emissions reductions from large buildings, is transforming the investment calculus for hotel owners in the market and providing a test case for similar regulation emerging globally.

The Forum hosts 250 attendees across a single intensive day, deliberately structured to maximise meaningful conversation. Morning sessions establish shared context; afternoon working groups develop specific recommendations; an evening dinner creates the informal connections that often prove most durable.

Workshop leaders include sustainability directors from major hotel groups, independent consultants who have overseen certification programmes at over 500 properties, and architects specialising in hotel renovation for environmental performance.

Registration is open to hotel operators, investors, developers, and technology providers working in the sustainability space. H1H community members receive preferential access and a 20 percent registration fee reduction.

metadata.title: TIAC Tourism Congress 2026
metadata.description: The Tourism Industry Association of Canada's annual Tourism Congress is the national gathering of Canada's tourism and hospitality sector, convening in...

records.body:
The Tourism Industry Association of Canada's annual Tourism Congress is the national gathering of Canada's tourism and hospitality sector, convening in Ottawa to engage directly with policymakers, regulators, and the industry associations that shape the operating environment for Canadian travel and hospitality businesses.

The Ottawa location is deliberate, the Congress is as much a policy engagement event as an industry conference. Delegates meet with federal ministers, departmental officials, and members of Parliament to advance the sector's priorities on visa processing, aviation access, infrastructure investment, and the regulatory frameworks that affect hotel development and operation across Canada.

The 2026 programme addresses the labour market outlook for Canadian hospitality, the federal government's international tourism attraction strategy, the investment case for indigenous tourism development, and the infrastructure gaps that constrain Canada's competitiveness as an international destination. The Congress closes with the Canadian Tourism Awards, the sector's most prestigious recognition programme, celebrating exceptional performance across fifteen categories spanning accommodation, attractions, destination management, and workforce development.
